newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields lower on foreign trends.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields lower on foreign trends.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were lower around midday on Tuesday, helped by stronger foreign markets.
"The focus is not on the domestic picture at the moment," a trader said. "We are following developments abroad and we have seen a small rebound this morning."
The ten-year bond yield fell three basis points to 6.83 percent, while the six-month T-bill slipped one to 4.20.
The crown benefited from a generally stronger dollar and strengthened to 4.4605 to the mark against 4.4855 crowns late on Monday.
Prices were not affected by the Riksbank leaving its key repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent as the decision was expected.
Players were focusing on the second half of U.S. Fed Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins speech on Wednesday but were not expecting any news.

German unemployment statistics on Thursday and U.S. employment figures on Friday were also likely to be watched carefully, dealers said. Players feared a high increase in German unemployment could make it difficult for the country to meet Maastricht criteria. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1071
